title: [iOS, Android] Free Premium Offline Plan Unlock for CardWarden (Loyalty & Gift Card Wallet, Was $9.99) @ App Store & Google Play

[garygaz] Yes
https://cardwarden.app/blog/why-i-built-cardwarden
[iori57] Nope. Built it with skills I picked up while working in a Startup company, mainly Kotlin Multiplatform and how to design and handle security architecture to handle user's data to ensure privacy. Loved Kotlin Multiplatform as it can use same business logic between Android and iOS to keep them as consistent as possible, with only minor differences, which is a blessing for indie devs like myself. Of course AI are being used intensively to speed up work, especially the UI, but every architecture decision is mine. Don't think any vibe coders would use Kotlin Multiplatform as it is fairly new and AI probably go straight with the more popular toolset from the get go.
I've been building mobile apps for over a decade, here's my credit card manager app built 10 years ago and still supporting today: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.thesimples…
The startup ran out of money, and everyone are out of jobs, some lucky ones managed to find a new job, while I'm still looking I'm building CardWarden as a passion project which I wanted to build for a long time but didn't get time to. At the same time preparing for AI job apocalypse in case I could never find another programming job, and have to work in other fields, at least my programming passion won't go to waste :)
Do let me know if anyone has opening for Android/iOS developer!
[silverham] Can the "offline" version backup to dropbox / google drive etc.?
[iori57] Yes, just export your data, and when asked where to save to, if you have dropbox and google drive installed, you can select from the left pane (Android workflow). iOS might be more manual though.
[Typhoon365] App sounds great for reward cards. Hope your credit card storage and transmission is fully PCI compliant, I would state this on your app so people know it follows the strict legal compliance for storage of credit card numbers.
[iori57] Thanks! Last I checked, PCI compliant is only needed if the app process payments, which the app doesn't. But thanks for reminder, I will double check again. Gift card and credit card numbers (and all sensitive data) are all encrypted before storage. If you lose the password as well as recovery phrase, then they are gone and no way to recover.
[custom] PCI also applies to storage of cards, not just processing of payments
[iori57] I'll see what I can do in the next update, thanks
[theguyrules] Damn, shame the family plan is paid but it's also fair.
[iori57] Thanks for understanding! I've priced the family plan to something I would pay myself when looking for such an app for my own use back in the day (and couldn't find one), and kept it low so more people can use it without breaking the bank.
Btw if you don't mind sharing all cards, cloud plan is sufficient - just login using the same account across multiple devices and everyone sees the same cards and updates synced automatically in real time with no manual intervention. Family plan is for when you need fine grain sharing - keep personal cards private, while only sharing selected cards. And role based permission. And Kids mode - allow kids to access the shared cards without an account.
Cheers

[F0rtitude] How does this compare with other gift card wallets like Tchecker and Cardvark?
[iori57] Each have their own strengths, I find their layout a bit complicated I prefer something simpler myself. (and of course I am not biased XD) As of this moment CardWarden has some of these strong points:
Requires the least click to reach the barcode compare to others (I could be wrong)
Supports attaching front and back image, as well as customize card face using any image (they would probably follow suite soon)
Seamless cloud sync and family card sharing (the differentiator, none other card wallet app in both App Store and Play Store has this) though this is a subscription outside of this promo
Home screen widget and smart watch support (actually not sure if they have)
Supports credit/debit cards (wanted to position CardWarden to support more card types other than limited to just loyalty and gift cards, or even boarding pass and apple .pkpass format etc)

When adding new GIFT or LOYALTY cards by editing the Cards tab, what are the minimum required fields?
[iori57] Better to add at least one of each gift and loyalty card with minimal fields before exporting it out to check.
Technically loyalty card only needs - name, templateId, barcodeFormat, cardNumber
and gift card only needs - name, templateId, barcodeFormat, cardNumber, initialBalance, currencyBalance, currencyCode
But the app also auto fills backgroundColor (it has a default), createdAt and updatedAt. So best to use a minimally filled row as a base when adding new.
By the way exportId in cards tab needs to be a unique guid.
You have such a unique use case.
